title: Object removal versus wrongful removal
question: Describe the removal of the item from the display. Does this footage prove wrongful removal or theft?

observable_evidence_log.observation: Subject in brown jacket and hair bun crouches near lower display shelf
Reaches into bottom shelf and grasps merchandise item
Lifts item off display while standing upright
Holds item securely against torso at waist height
Pivots body 180 degrees toward aisle exit corridor
Walks down aisle carrying item in right hand in plain view

reviewer_A.technical_assessment: Clear visual track of item extraction and movement along aisle. No concealing container or covert concealment motion observed.

reviewer_B.domain_rationale: Removing an item from a store display and carrying it is the standard method customers use to bring goods to checkout, or store associates use to restock. Calling this 'wrongful removal' without seeing an exit past checkout is an unsubstantiated accusation.
reviewer_B.evidentiary_status: Item movement is visible; wrongful intent or unauthorized possession is strictly unsupported by footage.

adjudication.adjudication_notes: Consensus reached: item removal from shelf is verified; 'wrongful' or 'theft' attribution is an unobservable legal conclusion.

provenance_disclosure: Modeled expert dual-reviewer protocol (CV Engineer & Loss Prevention Officer) developed for benchmark specification and rubric calibration; not biological crowd workers.
